senses.text: alphabetical letter The second letter of the alphabet: called baA='N and baA ; (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np ;) the latter of which forms is used in spelling; like as are its analogues, as tA [and vA ] and HA [and xA and rA ] and TA [and ZA and fA and hA ] and yA ; because in this case they are not generally regarded as nouns, but as mere sounds: (Sb, M:) [these are generally pronounced with imáleh, i. e. bé, té, &c., with the exception of HA , xA , TA , and ZA ; and when they are regarded as nouns, their duals are bayaAni , tayaAni , &c.:] the pl. of baA='N is baA='aAtN ; and that of baA is A^abowaA='N (TA ubi suprà.) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrah [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of those termed $afahiy~ap [or labial]; and of those ter

; or, as some say, it is fet-h when it is with a noun properly so called; as in mar~a bazayodK : so in the K; this being the reverse of what they have prescribed in the case of [the preposition] l : but in the case of b , no vowel but kesr is known. (MF.) It denotes the same in the saying bihi daA='N [ In him is a disease; i. e. a disease is cleaving to him ]: and so [accord. to some] in A^aqosamotu bA@ll~`hi [ I swore, or, emphatically, I swear, by God; and similar phrases, respecting which see a later division of this paragraph]. (L.) So, too, in A^a$oraka bA@ll~`hi , because meaning He associated another with God: and in wak~alotu bifulaAnK , meaning I associated a wakiyl [or factor &c.] with such a one. (T.) [And so in other phrases here following.] Ealayoka bizayodK Keep thou to Zeyd:

You say, AfotataHa AlbaAba Albar~aAniY~a He opened the outer door. (A.)

senses.text: 1 , [aor. , inf. n. generally buro'N or baraA='apN ,] He was, or became, clear, or free, of, or from, a thing; in the manners which will be explained below: (Bd ii. 51:) he was, or became, in a state of freedom or immunity, secure, or safe. (T.) [Hence,] bariy^a mina AlmaraDi , and baraA^a , (T, Msb,) aor. ; and baruw^a , aor. ; (Msb;) inf. n. buro'N : (T, Msb:) or bariy^a mn AlmrD , inf. n. buro'N , with damm; and the people of El-Hijáz say baraA^a , inf. n. baro'N , with fet-h: (S:) accord. to As, bariYa mn AlmrD is of the dial. of Temeem; and baraA^a of the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz: or, accord. to AZ, the people of El-Hijáz say baraA^a ; and the rest of the Arabs say bariy^a : (T:) or baraA^a [alone], said of a sick man, aor. and ; and bariy^a ; and baruw^a ; inf. n. baro'N [prob
; or sound, or healthy, at the close of disease, but was yet weak

; or he recovered, but not completely, his health and strength; syn. niqaha ; (M, K;) i. e., he acquired that slight degree of soundness, or health, which comes at the close of disease, but with disease remaining in him. (TA.) [And bariy^a Aljuroju , or baraA^a , The wound healed

; or became in a healing state: of frequent occurrence.] And bariy^a mina AlA^amori , [the only form of the verb used in this case, and in the other cases in which it is mentioned below,] aor. and , the latter extr., (M, K,) or rather it is very strange, for IKoot says that naEima , aor. yanoEumu , and faDila , aor. yafoDulu , are the only instances of this kind, (TA,) inf. n. baraA='apN (M, K) and baraA='N (Lh, M, K) and buruw^N , (M,) or buro'N , (K, TA,) or buruwo'N ; (CK;) and ↓ ; (S, * M, K, Mgh; *) [ He was, or became, free from the thing, or affair

; or clear, or quit, thereof; clear of having or taking, or of having had or taken, any part therein; guiltless of it: and also, irresponsible for it; as in an ex. q. v. voce EiDaADN :] said in relation to [a fault or the like, and] a debt, and a claim, and religion [&c.]. (Lh, M.) You say, bariy^a mina AlEayobi , (Mgh, Msb,) or AlEuyuwbi , (S,) inf. n. baraA='apN , (Mgh,) He was, or became, free (Msb) [ from the fault, defect, imperfection, blemish, or vice ], (Mgh, Msb,) [or faults, &c.]. (S.) And bariy^a mina Ald~ayoni , (T, Mgh, Msb,) or Ald~uyuwni , (S,) aor. , (T, Msb,) inf. n. baraA='apN , (T, Mgh, Msb,) He was, or became, clear, or quit, of the debt; (or debts; S;) irresponsible for it [or them ]: or in a state of immunity with respect to it [or them ]; i. e., exempt from the deman

; or exempt from the demand thereof; ] as also ↓ . (M.) And bariy^otu A_ilayoka mino fulaAnK , inf. n. baraA='pN , [ I was, or became, or have become, clear, to thee, of having or taking, or of having had or taken, any part with such a one

; or, irresponsible to thee for such a one: ] (AZ, T, S: * [in one copy of the S, I find the phrase bariy^otu minoka , commencing the art.; but not in other copies:]) this is the only form of the verb used in this case, and in relation to debt [and the like]. (AZ, T.) ― -b2- He removed himself, or kept, far, or aloof, [from unclean things, or things occasioning blame; followed by mino , with which it may be rendered he shunned, or avoided; ] syn. tanaz~ahu and tabaAEada . (T.) [You say, bariy^a mina AlA^aqo*aAri He removed himself, or kept, far, or aloof, from unclean things. ] ― -b3- He manifested an excuse, [or asserted himself to be clear or quit or irresponsible, like ↓ ,] and gave warning; syn. A^aEo*ara and A^ano*ara . (T.)

Hence, in the Kur [ix. 1], baraA='apN mina A@ll~`hi warasuwlihi A manifestation of excuse, and a warning, from God and his apostle. (T.) -A2- baraA^a A@ll~`hu Alxaloqa , (Fr, T, S, M, K,) or Alxaliyaqapa , (Msb,) aor. , (T, M, &c.,) inf. n. baro'N (T, S, M, K) and buruwo'N , (AZ, Lh, M, K,) God created mankind, or the beings, or things, that are created, syn. xalaqa , (Fr, T, M, Msb, K,) after no similitude, or model, (TA,) [ but, properly, though not always meaning so, out of pre-existing matter; for] Bd says [in ii. 51] that the primary meaning of the root br' is to denote a thing's becoming clear, or free, of, or from, another thing; either by being released [therefrom], as in bariy^a AlmariyDu mino maraDihi and Almadoyuwnu mino daynihi [both sufficiently explained above]

; or by production [therefrom], as in baraA^a A@ll~`hu A=dama mina AlT~iyni [ God produced, or created, Adam, from, or out of, clay ]. (TA.) This verb relates to substances [as in the exs. given above] and to accidents; and hence, [in the Kur lvii. 22,] mino qboli A^ano naboraA^ahaA [ Before our creating it, if hA refer to muSiybap , preceding it; but, as Bd says, it may refer to this, or to AlA^aroD , or to A^anofus ]: (M:) but Albaro'u has a more particular application than Alxaloqu ; the former being particularly applied to the creation of animate beings, with few exceptions: you say, baraA^a A@ll~`hu Aln~asamapa wa xalaqa Als~am`waAti waAlA^aroDa [ God created, or produced, man, or the soul, and He created the heavens and the earth ]. (TA.) [To this verb, or perhaps to baray , or to bo

2 , inf. n. tabory^apN : see 4, in four places. [Hence,] laA Alt~aboriy^api The lA that denies in a general manner, absolutely, or to the uttermost; i. e. the lA that is a universal negative. (Mughnee &c.) ― -b2- Also He verified his being free [from a thing], clear, or quit, [of it,] guiltless [of it], or irresponsible [for it]. (Mgh, TA.)

3 , (T, S, M, Mgh, K,) inf. n. mubaAraA^apN (T, M, Mgh) and biraA='N , (M,) He made him (his copartner) free, clear, quit, or irresponsible, the latter doing to him the same: (Mgh:) he compounded, or made a compromise, with him (his hired man, T, M) for their mutual separation: (M:) he separated himself from him (his copartner, S, O), the latter doing the same. (S, O, K.) And baAraA^otu Alr~ajula I became free, clear, quit, or irresponsible, to the man, he becoming so to me. (M.) And bArA^ AlmaroA^apa , (T, M, K,) or A@moraA^atahu , (S,) inf. n. as above, (M,) He compounded, or made a compromise, with the woman (or his wife, S) for their mutual separation; (M, K;) i. e. he divorced her for a compensation [ which she was to make him, such as her giving up a portion of her dowry remaining du

4 He (God, S, M, K) [ recovered him, or] restored him to convalescence, (M, K,) mina AlmaraDi [ from the disease, sickness, or malady ]. (S.) ― -b2- A^aboraA^aka mina AlA^amori and ↓ (M, K *) He (i. e. God, TA) made thee, pronounced thee, or held thee, or hath made thee, &c., or may He make thee, &c., to be free from the thing or affair, or clear or quit thereof, or guiltless thereof, or irresponsible for it; (TA;) [or He acquitted thee, or hath acquitted thee, or may He acquit thee, thereof

; or He showed thee, or hath showed thee, or may He show thee, to be free from it, &c.: see also 2, above:] said in relation to [a fault or the like, and] a debt, and a claim, and religion [&c.]. (M.) You say, mina AlEayobi ↓ I made him, pronounced him, or held him, to be free from the fault, defect, imperfection, blemish, or vice. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxiii. 69], ↓ A@ll~`hu mimaA qaAluwA (M) But God showed him to be clear of that which they said. (Bd.) You say also, A^aboraA^otuhu mina Ald~ayoni I made him, pronounced him, or held him, to be clear, or quit, of the debt; irresponsible for it

; or in a state of immunity with respect to it; i. e., exempt from the demand thereof: (Msb:) and A^aboraA^otuhu mim~aA liY Ealayohi ; and ↓ , inf. n. taboriy^apN ; [ I acquitted him of that which he owed me: ] (S:) and A^aboraA^otuhu [alone] I made him, pronounced him, or held him, to be clear, or quit, of a claim that I had upon him, or a due or right that he owed me. (Mgh.) -A2- AbrA^ [in the T (as on the authority of Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee) A^aboraY ] He entered upon [ the night, or day, called ] AlbaraA=' , q. v. (K.)
5 see 1, in three places. tbr~A^ minohu also signifies He asserted himself to be free from it
; or clear, or quit, of it; namely, a fault, or the like. (Mgh.) [And He declared himself to be clear of him; to be not connected, or implicated, with him; he renounced him: see Kur ii.
6 We separated ourselves, each from the other. (TA.) [See

10 , (T,) or AstbrA^ mina Albawoli , (Msb,) He took extraordinary pains, or the utmost pains, in cleansing the orifice of his penis from the remains of urine, by shaking it and pulling it and the like, until he knew that nothing remained in it: (T:) or he purified, or cleansed, himself from urine; syn. tanaz~ahu Eanohu : (Msb:) or AstbrA^ , (M,) or AstbrA^ Al*~akara , (K, TA,) signifies he took extraordinary pains, or the utmost pains, in cleansing the penis from urine

; or he cleansed it entirely from urine; (M, * K, * TA;) and so AstbrA^ Alfaroja : and in like manner, AstbrA^ti Alfaroja said of a woman: (El-Munáwee, TA:) but the lawyers make a distinction between AsotiboraA='N and AisotinoqaA='N [which are made syn. in the M and K]: see the latter word. (TA.) ― -b2- And AstbrA^ AljaAriyapa , (T, S, Mgh,) or AlmaroA^apa , (M, Msb, K,) He abstained from sexual intercourse (T, M, K) with the girl whom he had purchased or whom he had taken captive, (T,) or with the woman, (M, K,) until she had menstruated (T, M, K) at his abode, once, and then become purified: (T:) the meaning is, (T,) he sought to find her free from pregnancy. (T, Mgh, Msb.) ― -b3-

Hence, (Mgh,) AstbrA^ Al$~ayo'i , (Z, Mgh, Msb,) or AlA^amora , (TA,) He searched, searched out, or sought to find or discover, the uttermost of the thing, or affair, (Z, Mgh, Msb, TA,) in order that he might know it, (Mgh,) to put an end to his doubt. (Z, Mgh, Msb, TA.) You say, AisotaboraA^otu maA Einodaka [ I searched, or sought to find or discover, or I have searched, &c., the uttermost of what thou hast, of knowledge &c.]. (S, TA.) And AstbrA^ A^roDa ka*aA famaA wajada DaAl~atahu [ He searched the uttermost of such a land and found not his stray beast ]. (TA.) ; or, more commonly, I am clear, or quit, of it, or him ]; and minohu ↓ and xalaA='N minohu ; (S;) and minohu ↓ : (M:) and ↓ and AlxalaA='u [ We are clear, or quit, of you ]; (Fr, T;) i. e., *awuw AlbaraA='i : so says Aboo-Is-hák; and As says the like of what Fr says. (Bd.) bariYo'N occurs in several places in the Kur. (M.) Accord. to IAar, it signifies Clear of evil qualities or dispositions; shunning what is vain and false; remote from actions that occasion suspicion; pure in heart from associating any with God: and it signifies sound in body and intellect. (T.) See also baAriy^N , in two places.

A writing of [i. e. conferring] immunity or exemption: from bariy^a mina Ald~ayoni and AlEayob , of which it is the inf. n.: pl. baraAA=tN , with medd: baraAwaAtN is [pl. of baraApN , and both of these are] vulgar. (Mgh.)

; or, particularly, mankind; syn. Alxaloqu : (T, S, M:) pronounced without ' ; (T, S;) originally with ' , like nabiY~N and *ur~iyapN ; (M;) and the people of Mekkeh differ from the other Arabs in pronouncing these three words with ' : (Yoo, T, M:) Lh says that the Arabs agree in omitting the ' in these three instances; and he does not except the people of Mekkeh: (M:) it is of the measure faEiylapN in the sense of mafoEuwlapN , (Msb,) from baraA^a A@ll~`hu Alxaloqa , meaning xalaqahumo : (Fr, T:) or, if derived from AlbaraY [“earth” or “dust”], it is originally without ' : (Fr, T, S:) pl. baraAyaA and bariy~aAtN . His bed, or place of sleep, became cold; meaning] (tropical:) he went on a journey. ; or to the cessation of motion. (MF.) For ― -b4- barada , (MF,) aor. , (Mgh,) inf. n. barodN , (MF,) likewise signifies (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, still, quiet, or motionless; (Mgh, MF;) for instance, a slaughtered sheep or goat [&c.]. You say, ruEiba fabarada makaAnahu [(assumed tropical:) He became frightened, and remained motionless in his place; makaAnahu meaning fiY makaAnahu : and hence,] (tropical:) he became amazed, or stupified. senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. ba$amN , He (a man, S, TA, or an animal, Msb) suffered, or became affected with, indigestion, (S, Msb, K,) in consequence of much eating: (Msb:) or he was heavy in consequence of food: (Ham p. 363:) or he became distressed, or oppressed, by eating much food. (TA.) You say, ba$imotu mina AlT~aEaAmi I suffered indigestion from the food: (S:) or was heavy in consequence of the food. (Ham ubi suprà) And ba$ima AlfaSiylu mino kavorapi $urobi All~abani The young camel suffered indigestion from drinking much milk. (S.) Accord. to IDrd, ba$amN specially relates to beasts: accord. to Kh, it specially arises from greasy food. (Har p.

164.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) He became affected with disgust, aversion, loathing, or nausea. (S, K, TA.) You say, ba$imotu mina AlT~aEaAmi , (S,) or Eani AlTEAm , (TA,) (tropical:) I turned away with disgust from the food; was averse from it; loathed it; nauseated it. (S, TA.) And ba$ima AlfaSiylu Eani All~abani (assumed tropical:) [ The young camel turned away with disgust from the milk; was averse from it; &c.]. (K in art. dqE .)
4 It (food) caused him to suffer, or be affected with, indigestion: (S, K, * TA:) or (assumed tropical:) loathing, or nausea. (K.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. (S, K) and and , (K,) inf. n. bugaAmN (JK, S, K) and buguwmN ; (JK, K;) and ↓ ; (K;) She (a gazelle) uttered a cry: (S:) or uttered her softest, or gentlest, cry (JK, K) to her young one: (K:) and sometimes it is said of a [wild] cow: (TA:) so too bagama said of a male gazelle: and the verb is also used transitively, said of a female gazelle uttering this cry to her young one. (JK.)

Also, (S, K,) ↓ both verbs, (K,) She (a camel) uttered a cry without clearness: (S:) or uttered a broken, or an interrupted, not a prolonged, yearning cry, to, or for, her young one: (K:) or uttered a weak cry, below that [ grumbling cry ] which is termed rugaA=' . (Ham p.

233.) [See an ex. in a verse of Dhu-rRummeh cited voce A_il~aA .] And bagama and ↓ said of the vayotal and A_iy~al and waEil , [all of which words are said to signify the mountain goat,] He uttered a cry. (K.) ― -b2- bagamahu , (S, K,) and bagama lahu , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He spoke to him obscurely, not expressing clearly to him the meaning of his speech to him; (S, K;) taken from the bugaAm of the she-camel; because it is a cry not uttered clearly. (TA.)

3 bAgmhu , (K,) inf. n. mubaAgamapN , (S,) (tropical:) He talked with him with a soft, or gentle, voice: (S, K, TA:) or AlmubaAgamapN is like AlmunaAgamapu , and means the speaking [ with another ] faintly; taken from the bugaAm [see 1] of the gazelle and the she-camel: (Ham p. 233:) or the holding amatory and enticing talk, or conversation, with another, with a soft, or gentle, voice. (TA.)
5 see 1, in three places.

6 [ tabaAgamato They (gazelles) uttered cries, or their softest or gentlest cries, one to another. ] One says, mararotu birawoDapK tatabaAgamu fiyhaA AlZ~ibaA='u [ I passed by a meadow in which the gazelles were uttering cries, &c., one to another ]: and bigizolaAnK yatabaAgamona [ by gazelles uttering cries, &c., one to another ]. (TA.)

A thing like the qilaAdap , [ a necklace, ] with which women ornament themselves. (TA.) [But this is apparently post-classical, from the Turkish buwgomaqo . In the present day, it is applied to A necklace of pearls. ]

A female gazelle uttering, or that utters, the cry termed bugaAm . (S, K.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A woman having a soft, or gentle, voice. (JK, TA.)

A young gazelle, and a young camel, to which the cry termed bugaAm is addressed by its mother. (JK.) ― -b2- One says, also, bugaAmN maboguwmN [ A cry &c. uttered ]; like as one says, qawolN maquwlN . (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. bugaA='N , (S, Mgh, K, &c.,) or this is a simple subst., and the inf. n. is bagoYN , (Msb,) [but, if this be correct, the former is generally used for the latter,] and bugFY , (Lh, K,) but the first is better known, and is the chaste form, and some say, bigFY , (TA,) and bugoyapN and bigoyapN , (K,) accord. to Th, but others hold these two to be simple substs., and some mention also bagoyapN , with fet-h, (TA,) and bugaAyapN , (As, S, TA,) He sought; sought for, or after; sought, desired, or endeavoured, to find, and take, or get; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.;) a stray-beast, (As, S, TA,) or any other thing, (S, Mgh, * Msb, * K, * TA,) good or evil; (Lh, TA;) as also ↓ and ↓ (S, Msb, K) and ↓ : (K:) or ↓ signifies he sought, &c., diligently, studiously, se

; or sought to do him evil ]. (S and K in art. Eqb .) ― -b2- And bagaAhu He sought, &c., a thing for him; like bagaY lahu . (Lh, Mgh, * K. *) You say, bagaAhu Al$~aYo'a He sought, &c., the thing for him; (S, K;) as also Al$~aYo'a ↓ : (K:) thus you say, AiboginiY ka*aA or k*A ↓ and Aiboga liY k*A Seek thou for me such a thing; (TA;) and DaAl~atiY ↓ Seek thou for me my stray-beast: (Mgh:) or Al$~aY'a ↓ signifies He aided, or assisted, him to seek the thing: (Ks, K:) or ka*aA ↓ signifies Seek thou for me such a thing; and also Aid thou me to seek such a thing. (JK.) It is said in the Kur [ix. 47], yaboguwnakumu Alfitonapa They seek, or desire, for you discord, or dissension
; or they seeking, &c.: and in the same [iii. 94], taboguwnahaA EiwajFA Ye seek, or desire, for it, namely, the way [of God], crookedness
; or ye seeking, &c.: the first objective complement of the verb being in the accus. case because of the suppression of the preposition l . (TA.) ― -b3- [
Hence, app.,] bagaAniY daA='F It procured to me disease; it caused disease to befall me. (Ham p.

794.) And A_in~ahu la*uw bugaAyapK Verily he is one who makes much gain: (JK, K:) but in the M, *uw bugaAyapK lilokasobi , meaning a seeker of gain. (TA.) And maAbugiYa lahu Good was not appointed to betide him. (TA.) ― -b4- bagaY EalaY A^axiyhi , inf. n. bagoYN , He envied his brother; he wished that a blessing, or cause of happiness, or an excellence, might become transferred from his brother to himself: so says Lh, who holds this to be the primary signification of the verb. (TA.) It is said in a prov., AlbagoYu EiqaAlu Aln~aSori [ Envy is the shackle of aid from God against an enemy or a wrongdoer]. (TA.) ― -b5-

Hence, (Lh, TA,) bagoYN signifies The acting wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically; (Lh, S, TA;) because the envier so acts towards the envied; his endeavour being to cause, by guile, the blessing of God upon him to depart from him: (Lh, TA:) or the seeking, or endeavouring, to act corruptly, wrongly, or unjustly: (Az, TA:) or the exceeding the due bounds, or just limits, in any way: (S:) accord. to Er-Rághib, it is of two kinds: one of these is approved, and this is the passing beyond the bounds of equity to exercise beneficence, and beyond the bounds of obligatory duties to do what is not obligatory: the other is disapproved, and this is the passing beyond the bounds of that which is true, or right, to do that which is false, or wrong, or to do acts of a doubtful nature: but in most i
Also, aor. , (TA,) inf. n. bagoYN , (Az, TA,) He magnified himself

; or behaved proudly, haughtily, or insolently: (Az, TA:) because he who does so passes beyond the bounds of his proper station to a station that does not belong to him. (TA.) ― -b6- And [hence,] bagaY fiY mi$yatihi , (K,) inf. n. bagoYN , (TA,) He [app. a horse, and perhaps a man also,] was proud, or self-conceited, and quick, in his gait: (K:) or bagoYN in a horse, (S, TA,) or in the running of a horse, (JK, TA,) is the being proud, or self-conceited, with exceeding briskness or liveliness or sprightliness. (JK, S, TA.) ― -b7- And bagati Als~amaA='u , (S, K,) inf. n. bagoYN , (TA,) The sky rained vehemently: (A'Obeyd, S, K:) or exceeded, in rain, the limit of what was wanted. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And bagaY AlwaAdiY The valley flowed with water reaching to a place to which it had not reached
, in the Kur [xii. 65], is said to mean We do not lie: and we do not act wrongfully: or it may mean what do we seek, or desire? (TA.) ― -b2-

Also, (K,) inf. n. bagoYN , (TA,) He looked at a thing [ to see ] how it was; (K;) and so bagaA , inf. n. bagowN : mentioned by Kr. (TA.) ― -b3- And, (K,) with the same inf. n., (TA,) He looked, watched, or waited, for a person or thing. (Kr, K.)

(TA in art. bwg .)

4 see 1, in five places. ― -b2- AbgAhu Al$~aYo'a also signifies He made him, or caused him, to seek the thing; to seek for it, or after it; to seek, or desire, or endeavour, to find, and take, or get, it. (S.)

[originally an inf. n. (see 1)] Much of rain

; or much rain: in [some of] the copies of the K, AlbTr is erroneously put for AlmTr : (TA:) [and in some, AlbagiY~u for AlbagoYu : in a MS. copy, I find AlbagiY~u Alkaviyru mina AlmaTari : and in the CK, AlbagiY~u Alkaviyoru mn Aln~aZari :] or bagoYu Als~amaA='i signifies the main portion, (As, S,) or the vehemence, and the main portion, (Lh, JK, TA,) of the rain of the sky. We drove away the main portion, or the vehemence, and the main portion, of the rain of the sky behind us or from us; meaning it was driven away behind us or from us, or it departed; as is shown in art. dfE ].

and ↓ (JK, S, Msb, K) and ↓ (K) A thing sought; (JK, K;) as also ↓ [originally an inf. n. (see 1)]: (JK:) or a thing wanted, needed, or required; an object of want or need; a want, or needful or requisite thing or affair: (S, Msb:) as in the saying, liY fiYbaniY fulaAnK bagoyapN and bugoyapN [ I have among the sons of such a one an object of want ]: (S:) or the first signifies a state that one seeks; and the second, a thing itself that one wants: (As, S, Msb: *) and the first, (JK,) or third, (K,) signifies also a stray beast that is sought: (JK, K:) the pl. of the second is bugFY . , accord. to some, of the measure faEiylN ; accord. to others, of the measure faEuwlN , originally baguwYN ; [if of the former, originally meaning “ sought; ” and if of the latter, originally meaning “ seeking; ”] and therefore [in either case] not admitting the affix p : (TA:) A fornicatress, an adulteress, or a prostitute; (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ [of the measure faEuwlN , and therefore anomalous, like nahuw~N ]: (M, K:) bagiY~N is not applied to a man, (Lh, Msb,) nor bagiy~apN to a woman: (Lh, TA:) pl. bagaAyaA . (S, Mgh, Msb.) [See an ex. voce mahorN .] ― -b2- Also A female slave, (JK, S, K,) whether she be a fornicatress or an adulteress or a prostitute or not; (TA;) not meant to imply revilement, though originally applied to female slaves because of their prostitution of thems

Also, pl. bagaAyaA : see bagiY~N , last sentence.

Seeking; seeking for, or after; seeking, desiring, or endeavouring, to find, and take, or get: pl. bugaApN and bugoyaAnN (K) and bug~aA='N . (TA: [there mentioned as a pl., but not said to be of baAgK , nor explained.]) baAgK wahaAdK , lit. A seeker of [stray] camels and a guide of the way, mentioned in a trad. respecting the Hijreh (as said by A booBekr to a man who asked him “ Who are ye? ”), alludes to the seeking of religion and the guiding from error. (TA.) One says, far~iquwA lih`*ihi AlA_ibili bugoyaAnFA yuDib~uwna lahaA , i. e. [ Disperse ye, for these camels, seekers ] to scatter themselves in search thereof. (S.) ― -b2- Acting wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically, [&c.,] towards others: pl. bugaApN . (Msb. [See

1.]) gayora baAgK , in the Kur ii. 168, [&c.,] means Not being a revolter from the Muslims, (Jel,) or, against the Imám: (TA:) or it means not desiring to eat for the sake of enjoyment: or not seeking to exceed the limit of his want: (Az, TA:) or not seeking what he should not seek. (Er-Rághib, TA.) fiy^apN baAgiyahN A company of men revolting from the just Imám. (K.) firoqapN baAgiyapN A party occupying itself with corrupt, wrong, or unjust, conduct. (Msb.) ― -b3- A camel that does not impregnate, or get with young. (Kr, K.) ― -b4- A horse that is proud, or self-conceited, with exceeding briskness or liveliness or sprightliness: (JK, Ham p. 210:) [but] Kh disallows its being thus used. (S.) -A2- [The pl.] bugoyaAnN also signifies What the sportsman, or hunter, seeks, of game, or objects o
: see what next precedes.
, (K,) or, as in the Tekmileh, Almutabag~iY , (TA,) The lion: (K:) because he is always seeking prey. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (JK, M,) aor. yabiq~u ; and baq~a , [first pers. baqiqotu ,] aor. yabaq~u [in the TA yabuq~u , which, being anomalous, is probably a mistake,] inf. n. baq~N and baqaqN [which is of the latter verb accord. to analogy] and baqiyqN ; (M;) He spoke, or talked, much; was, or became, loquacious; (JK, M, TA;) as also ↓ (JK, S, M, TA) and ↓ . (M, TA.) And baq~a kalaAmFA [in which case the aor., accord. to rule, unless the noun be a specificative, is yabuq~u ,] and baq~a bikalaAmK [ He was, or became, profuse in speech ]. (M.) And baq~a EalaY Alqawomi , (Zj, K,) or baq~a kalaAmahu , (M,) inf. n. baq~N and baqaAqN , (K,) He spoke, or talked, much against the people, or company of men; (Zj, M, * K;) as also ↓ . (K.)

Hence, (TA,) qado malaA^ota AlA^aroDa baqaAqFA [ Thou hast filled the earth, or land, with much discoursing ], said, in dispraise, to a voluminous writer. (M, TA.) ― -b2- baq~ato and ↓ , said of a woman, She had many children: (JK, S, M, K:) or, as Sb says, baq~ato waladFA she brought forth many children. (M, TA.) ― -b3- baq~ati Als~amaA='u , (S, M, K,) and ↓ , (M, TA,) The sky rained much, and consecutively, or uninterruptedly: (M, TA: *) or rained vehemently. (S, M, K.) ― -b4- baq~a , (M, K,) aor. yayaq~u , (M,) or yabiq~u , (TA,) inf. n. baq~N , (M, TA,) He gave largely, or amply: (IF, M, K, * TA:) in some of the copies of the K, AlEaZamap is erroneously put for AlEaTiy~ap . (TA.) And baq~a lanaA AlEaTaA='a He made the gift large, or ample, to us. (M.) ― -b5- baq~a maAlahu He distribute

Hence, (M,) baq~a EiyaAbahu , (M, L, TA,) in the K, erroneously, EiyaAlahu , (TA,) He spread out (K, TA) his [ receptacles of skin, or leather, termed ] EyAb , and put forth, or took forth, what was in them. (TA.) ― -b8- He clave, slit, ripped, or rent, the thing. (JK.) So in the phrase baq~a AljiraAba [ He slit, ripped, or rent, and opened, (see maboquwqN ,) the bag, or receptacle, for travelling-provisions &c. ]. (K.) ― -b9- baq~a , (IF, K,) inf. n. buquwqN , (TA,) said of a plant, [app. from its cleaving the earth,] It came forth. (IF, K, TA.) -A2- baq~a AlmakaAnu , [aor., app., yabiq~u , or yabaq~u ,] The place abounded with baq~ [i. e. gnats, or musquitoes
; or bugs ]; as also ↓ . (M, TA.)

4 see 1, in five places. ― -b2- Abq~ waladu fulaAnK , inf. n. A_iboqaAqN , The children of such a one multiplied; became many, or numerous. (TA.) ― -b3- A^abaq~ati Alganamu fiY Aljadobi , accord. to the K, (TA,) or ↓ Alganamu fiY EaAmi jadobK , (JK, and thus in the O, TA,) The ewes, or she-goats, being lean, or meagre, brought forth [ in drought, or scarcity, or in a year of drought or scarcity ]. (JK, O, K, TA.) — Abq~ AlwaAdiY The valley put forth its plants, or herbage. (O, L, TA.) In the K, xaraja baqaAqupu is erroneously put for xaraja nabaAtuhu . (TA.) ― -b4- A^abaq~ahumo xayorFA , or $ar~FA , He did to him much, or ample, good, or evil. (Ibn-'Abbád, JK, K.)

1 , (S, M,) biAlmaA='i , (M,) [inf. n. baqobaqapN , q. v. infrà,] The mug made a [ guggling or gurgling ] sound with the water [ on being dipped into it or on one's pouring out from it ]. (S, * M.) And baqobaqati Alqidoru The cooking-pot boiled [ so as to make a sound of bubbling ]. (M.) ― -b2- See also
1. ― -b3- baqobaqa EalayonaA AlkalaAma i. q. far~aqahu [lit. He scattered speech (app. meaning he jabbered ) at us, or against us: compare baq~a EalaY Alqawomi , or baq~a kalaAmahu , above]. (K.)

: see baqaAqN . ― -b2- baq~apN A woman having many children: (Ibn-'Abbád, JK, K:) and ↓ a woman that brings forth many children. (M, TA.) ― -b3- A^avarN baq~N [ A trace, mark, track, impression, or the like, ] that is plainly apparent, or conspicuous. (JK, TA.) -A2-

Also, a pl. n.; (S, TA;) [or rather a coll. gen. n.;] sing., (S, TA,) or n. un., (JK, M, Msb, K, *) baq~apN ; (JK, S, M, &c.;) Gnats, or musquitoes; syn. baEuwDN : (S, M, K: *) or large baEuwD : (JK, M, Msb:) the poet 'Abder-Rahmán Ibn-El-Hakam, cited by IB, speaks of their singing [or humming]. (TA.) yaA Eayona baq~apK [ O eye of a gnat or musquito ] denotes smallness of the person of him to whom it is said
; or of the eye, as being likened to the eye of the gnat or musquito. (Har p.
619. [See an ex. voce Huzuq~N .]) ― -b2-

Also, [in the M is here added “ it is said, ” but this implies uncertainty where none exists,] A kind of insect, [namely, bugs, ] (M, K,) resembling the louse, (M, TA,) [ but larger, ] wide, (K,) red, and stinking, (M, K,) [and hence termed baq~N munotinN ,] found in bed-frames, or couch-frames, and in walls, [and therefore termed baq~u Alxa$abi and baq~u AlHiyTaAni ,] (M, TA,) called also banaAtu AlHaSiyri [from being found in mats]; (TA;) when one kills them, he smells [ what resembles ] the odour of bitter almonds proceeding from them. (M, L.) ― -b2- And baliduwA , aor. ; (M, K;) and baladuwA , aor. ; (K;) or the latter is correctly ↓ ; (M, * TA;) They kept to the ground, fighting upon it: (M, K:) said to be derived from bilaAdu AlA^aroDi . senses.text: 1 [inf. n. of balaga ] and A_ibolaAgN [inf. n. of ↓ , but it seems that AblAg is here a mistranscription for balaAgN , which is, like buluwgN , an inf. n. of balaga , and this observation will be found to be confirmed by a statement immediately following this sentence,] signify The reaching, attaining, arriving at, or coming to, the utmost point of that to which, or towards which, one tends or repairs or betakes himself, to which one directs his course, or which one seeks, pursues, endeavours to reach, desires, intends, or purposes; whether it be a place, or a time, or any affair or state or event that is meditated or intended or determined or appointed: and sometimes, the being at the point thereof: so says Abu-1-Kásim in the Mufradát. (TA: [in which it is said, in the supplement to the p

22 &c., He attained his manly vigour, or full maturity, &c.]. (TA.) And in balagaA^arobaEiyna sanapF [Kur xlvii. 14, He attained the age of forty years ]. (TA.) And in balaga maEahu Als~aEoYa [Kur xxxvii. 100, He attained to working with him ]. (TA.) In the Kur [iii. 35], occurs the phrase, waqado balaganiYa Alkibaru [ When old age hath come to me, or overtaken me ]: and in another place [xix. 9], wa qado balagotu mina Alkibari Eutiy~FA [ And I have reached the extreme degree of old age: so explained in the Expos. of the Jel]: phrases like A^adorakaniYa Aljahodu and A^adorakotuhu . (Er-Rághib, TA.) You say also, maA balaga ↓ with the accus. case as a denotative of state; meaning [ That clave to him, or adhered to him, &c.,] rising to its highest degree or point; from balaga Almanozila , ex

; or it came to my knowledge, &c.: and in this case it is generally followed by A^an~a , or by A^ano as a contraction of A^an~a : for exs., see these two particles. And in like manner, balaganiY Eanohu Information has come to me, or information came to me, from him, or concerning him, that such a thing has happened, or had happened.] And balaga said of a letter or writing, inf. n. balaAgN and buluwgN , It reached, arrived, or came. (Msb.) And said of a plant, or of herbage, It attained its full growth: (TA:) and of a tree, such as a palm-tree &c., its fruit became ripe: (AHn, TA:) and of fruit, it became ripe. (Msb.)

Also, said of a boy, (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. buluwgN , or, as IKoot says, balaAgN , (Msb,) He attained to puberty, virility, ripeness, or maturity; syn. A^adoraka , (T, S, Msb, K,) and AiHotalama ; (M, Msb;) and attained a consummate degree of goodliness ( balaga mina Aljawodapi mabolagFA ): (O, TA:) as though he attained the time of the writing of his marriage-contract, and of his having duties or obligations imposed upon him: (TA:) and in like manner one says of a girl, balaga , (T, TA,) or balagato . (TA.) ― -b2- balaga A@ll~`hu bihi [ God caused him to reach, attain, arrive at, or come to, his appointed end, or term of life; A^ajalahu , or the like, being understood]. (TA.) And bl~ghu maqoSuwdahu He caused him to attain his object of aim or endeavour &c.] And bal~agotu Alr~isaAlapa [ I brought, conveyed, or delivered, the message ]. (S.) And bl~ghu Als~alaAma , (Msb,) and Alxabara , (TA,) as also ↓ , (Msb, TA,) He brought, conveyed, delivered, or communicated, to him the salutation, (Msb,) and he brought, &c., or told, to him the news, or information. ; or an intensive epithet: as $akuwrN “ very thankful, ” or “ very grateful; ” and Ham~aAdN “ a great praiser, ” or “ a frequent praiser. ”]

; or a waterless desert: (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) or one that is plain, or level, in which horses are made to run: (M:) or one wherein is nothing: (TA:) so called, accord. to IJ, because it [often] destroys him who alights, or sojourns, in it: (M, Msb: *) or a plain tract, slightly elevated, with few trees, and without herbage, extending to the distance of a day's journey, or half a day's journey, or less, rugged and hard, and only in a country of mould, or clay: (ISh:) pl. biyodN : (S, M, Msb, K:) it has a pl. of a form proper to epithets because it is originally an epithet: (M:) by rule it should be bayodaAwaAtN . 250.) 250.) [See also art. bld . ; or midst, or main part, of the abode thereof: (S, TA:) the principal place of abode ( A^aSol ) thereof; (M, TA;) the place that comprises them; the place of their government, or regal dominion; and the seat of their dEwp [i. e. diEowap or kindred and brotherhood ]: (TA:) the midst of them: (M:) or, as some say, their [ kinsfolk such as are termed ] Ea$iyrap : (TA:) but when you say, A^ataAhumu AlEaduw~u fiY bayoDatihimo , the meaning is [ the enemy came to them in ] their principal place of abode ( A^aSol ), and the place where they were congregated. And bayoDapu AlqayoZi (tropical:) The most vehement, or intense, heat of summer, or of the hottest period of summer, from the [ auroral ] rising of Ald~abaraAn to that of suhayol ; [i. e., reckoning for the commencement of the era of the Flight, in central Arabia, from about the 26th of May to about the 4th of August, O. S.; ] (A, * TA;) as also AlqayoZi ↓ . (A, TA.) And bayoDapu AlS~ayofi (assumed tropical:) The main part of the Syf [or summer ]: (M, TA:) or the vehement, or intense, heat thereof. (Ham p.

Whiteness; contr. of sawaAdN ; in an animal, and in a plant, and in other things; and, accord. to IAar, in water also; (M;) the colour of that which is termed A^aboyaDu : (S, Msb, * K:) they said bayaADN and ↓ , (S, M, K,) like as they said manozilN and manozilapN : (S:) bayaADapN being applied to a whiteness in the eye. ; or exposed it to sale: (S, K:) and ↓ , as well as baAEahu , signifies he bought it. (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K.) The primary signification of bayoEN is The exchanging, or exchange, of property

; or the making an exchange with property; as in the phrases bayoEN raAbiHN [ an exchange of property bringing gain ], and bayoEN xaAsirN [ an exchange of property occasioning loss ]: and this is a proper signification when it relates to real substances: but it is tropically used to signify the making the contract [ of sale and purchase ]; because this is the means of giving [and obtaining] possession: [though this signification is what is termed HaqiyqapN Eurofiy~apN , i. e., a sense so common as to be conventionally regarded as proper:] the phrase SaH~a AlbayoEu , or baTala , and the like, mean Safoqapu AlbayoEi ; [i. e. The contract of sale, or purchase, was valid, or was null; ] but the prefixed n. being suppressed, and its complement [alone] used for it, and this being masc., the verb

131.)] ― -b3- You say also, baAEahu mina Als~uloTaAni , [lit. He sold him to the Sultán, ] meaning (tropical:) he slandered him, or calumniated him, to the Sultán.
